card: Adds a scheduled weekly GitHub Actions workflow to check the Windows code signing certificate for expiration within 90 days or revocation via CRL, opening a repository issue if replacement is needed. Bitcoin Core currently has no automated monitoring for signing certificates, relying on release candidate cycles to discover expiration. The author notes that relying on regular release cycles risks delaying short-notice bugfix releases. Duplicate issues are prevented by checking for existing reports.
changed_since_previous: Added CRL fetching and revocation verification to the check script using openssl verify, allowing the weekly monitor to report confirmed certificate revocations ahead of expiry while ignoring transient network failures.
evidence: PR description notes developers 'previously "relied on Release Candidates" as a dry-run for codesigners to realise that a certificate has expired and have time to fix it' and that this 'might not be appropriate in the future if we release more bugfix minor/patch releases on short notice.'
problem: Bitcoin Core lacks automated monitoring for code signing certificate validity and expiration, historically relying on release candidate cycles for code signers to notice expired certificates. If a minor or bugfix release needs to be published on short notice, an undetected expired or revoked certificate risks delaying the release.

risk.why: A bug in the workflow or script could file erroneous GitHub issues or fail to notice an expired certificate, but cannot impact node binaries or runtime behavior.

summary: Adds a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow and helper script that runs weekly to verify the validity, revocation status, and expiration date of the Windows code signing certificate. If the certificate is revoked, within 90 days of expiry, or expired, the workflow opens a GitHub issue detailing the certificate status and the checked commit.
